newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares slip in quiet post-Eid trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares slip in quiet post-Eid trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped a fraction on Sunday in a quiet trading day, the first since the market's three-day holiday for the Moslem feast of Eid al-Adha.
"Trade was very thin because most people are still on vacation," said Mohammed Hossny of Triple A Securities.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index fell 1.24 points to 387.98. from 389.22 last Wednesday.

Turnover was 69.69 million pounds ($20.5 million) but 44.90 million of this was in Alexandria Commercial and Maritime Bank . Brokers said the state sold these shares to the employees as part of the bank's partial privatisation.
In the open market, the most active share was fertiliser company Egyptian Financial and Industrial, which ended 5.00 pounds down at 216.00 in trade worth 4.14 million.

A one-off sale of 15,000 shares at 210.00 pounds also gave Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries a place among the busiest. Brokers said they did not know who was behind the transaction.
Cements and mills, two of the market's dominant sectors, ended mixed in thin trade.
Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA shed 0.50 pounds to close at 79.00 but Amriyah Cement gained 0.65 to 88.95.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills lost 1.39 to 99.16 pounds but East Delta Flour Mills rose 0.49 to end the day at 76.99. Other mills were mostly stable.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 593.13 points from 601.74 on Wednesday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 270.25 from 269.31.
Of the 77 shares traded, 24 advanced and 31 declined. The remaining 22 ended unchanged.
